plugins.name: Auto-format
plugins.description: Runs a formatter over every file the agent writes, chosen by extension: prettier, rustfmt, black and gofmt out of the box, or your own commands. The card says which files were formatted.

config.label: Formatters by extension
config.description: Comma-separated extensions to a command; $FILE is the written file.

plugins.author: Drift

plugins.name: Git auto-commit
plugins.description: Commits after every file the agent writes, so each change is its own revertible step and nothing is lost if a turn goes wrong. Only the written files are staged unless you choose to stage everything.

config.label: Stage every change
config.description: Stage the whole tree rather than only the written files.

plugins.author: Drift

plugins.name: Git context
plugins.description: Puts the repository's state beside each prompt: the branch, which files are changed, and the last five commits, so the model knows where it is without running git first.
plugins.author: Drift

plugins.name: Guard
plugins.description: Refuses shell commands that rewrite history (force pushes, hard resets, clean), notes failed commands under their output, and runs your tests when a reply ends with @guard test, keeping the turn going until they pass.

config.label: Test command
config.description: Program and arguments, run in the workspace when a reply says @guard test.

config.label: Time limit (ms)
config.description: The test run is stopped past this.

config.label: Refused commands
config.description: A shell line containing any of these is refused.

plugins.author: Drift

plugins.name: Lint check
plugins.description: Runs a type checker or linter after the agent writes a matching file and puts the problems in front of the model with the tool's output, so it fixes them in the same turn instead of leaving them for you.

config.label: Checks
config.description: Each check names the extensions it runs for and the command; $FILE is the written file.

plugins.author: Drift

plugins.name: Notify
plugins.description: Tells you when Drift needs you or has finished: a notice in the app when a call waits for your approval, and optionally a webhook (Slack, Discord, anything that takes JSON) when a turn ends, so you hear about it away from the screen.

config.label: Webhook URL
config.description: Posted JSON with text and content fields; leave empty for in-app notices only.

plugins.author: Drift

plugins.name: Protect files
plugins.description: Keeps the agent out of files a person should edit: .env and other secrets, keys and certificates, lockfiles, and the .git directory. Edits, writes and patches to a protected path are refused with the reason, and so is a shell line that would change one (a redirection, rm, mv, sed, git and the like); reading it is fine.

config.label: Protected paths
config.description: Globs: * within a folder, ** across folders, ? one character. A pattern without a slash matches the file name anywhere.

plugins.author: Drift

plugins.name: Test gate
plugins.description: Runs your test suite before any turn that changed files is allowed to end. Failures go back to the model as a prompt and it keeps working until they pass; a passing run leaves a line under the reply.

config.label: Test command
config.description: Program and arguments, run in the workspace.

config.label: Time limit (ms)
config.description: The run is stopped past this.

plugins.author: Drift

plugins.name: Tool log
plugins.description: Keeps a record of every tool call the agent makes: one JSON line per call in a file under the workspace, bounded so it never grows without limit, and optionally posted to an endpoint of yours.

config.label: Log file
config.description: Under the workspace. Set to false to keep no file.

config.label: Endpoint
config.description: Each call is POSTed here as JSON; leave empty for none.

plugins.author: Drift

plugins.name: Superpowers
plugins.description: A structured development workflow: brainstorm the problem first, write a plan, then execute it step by step with test-driven development, systematic debugging and verification before anything is called done. Skills trigger when relevant, so you rarely call them by name.
plugins.author: Jesse Vincent (obra)

plugins.name: Skills for Real Engineers
plugins.description: Matt Pocock's small, focused skills for disciplined engineering with AI: grill-me interviews you one question at a time until an idea is fully thought through, to-spec, to-tickets and implement turn it into work, plus code review, TDD, diagnosing bugs, PRs and more.
plugins.author: Matt Pocock

plugins.name: Agent Skills
plugins.description: Addy Osmani's full software lifecycle in skill form: spec, plan, build incrementally, test, review on five axes, simplify, and ship, with context engineering, security hardening, debugging and documentation along the way.
plugins.author: Addy Osmani

plugins.name: Karpathy Guidelines
plugins.description: A short set of coding guidelines from Andrej Karpathy's observations about common LLM coding mistakes, applied quietly: surface assumptions instead of guessing, the minimum code that solves the problem, surgical changes that leave adjacent code alone, and a definition of done to verify against.
plugins.author: forrestchang

plugins.name: SQL Server Query Plans
plugins.description: Reads SQL Server execution plans the way an experienced tuner would, from Erik Darling's own query tuning knowledge: what is actually slow and why, not which operators look expensive. Point the agent at a .sqlplan or .xml file and ask what is wrong.
plugins.author: Erik Darling
